original_question: Given a Coxeter system (W,S) and u <= v in W, construct an explicit combinatorial model for the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q), namely a set M(u,v) and statistic s : M(u,v) -> N such that P_{u,v}(q) = sum_{a in M(u,v)} q^{s(a)}, in a genuinely combinatorial rather than merely recursive way.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1.10: "Find a combinatorial interpretation for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials." More explicitly, for a Coxeter system (W,S) and u,v in W with u <= v, produce in some explicit combinatorial way a set M(u,v) and a function s:M(u,v)->N such that P_{u,v}(q)=sum_{a in M(u,v)} q^{s(a)}.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s actual target as the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial problem (not the parabolic or combinatorial-invariance problems), uses the right data M(u,v) and statistic s, states the generating-function identity in the same form as equation (1.4), and captures the nearby contextual emphasis that the desired model should be explicitly combinatorial rather than merely recursive.
missing_details: The official problem is universally quantified: it asks for such a construction for every Coxeter system (W,S) and every pair u,v in W with u <= v, not just for a fixed instance.

To be stand-alone, the question should specify that P_{u,v}(q) is the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial of W, i.e. P_{u,v}:=P^{emptyset,-1}_{u,v}=P^{emptyset,q}_{u,v}, as introduced from the parabolic theory in Theorem 1.3.
The ambient coefficient ring should be stated: P_{u,v}(q) lies in Z[q], with q an indeterminate; the target is not a formal power series or a polynomial over another field.
The underlying order and length notation should be made explicit: <= is Bruhat order on W, [u,v]={z in W : u <= z <= v}, and l(u,v)=l(v)-l(u).

If one wants the statement to be fully self-contained, one should record the normalizing facts from Theorem 1.3 that characterize P_{u,v}: P_{u,u}=1, P_{u,v}=0 if u not<= v, and deg P_{u,v} < (1/2) l(u,v) for u < v.

The paper’s phrasing is "in some explicit combinatorial way"; your phrase "genuinely combinatorial rather than merely recursive" is justified by the following discussion, but it is not itself the official wording of the problem statement.

The nearby discussion makes clear that a recursively defined M(u,v) of Deodhar type does not generally count as the sought combinatorial interpretation, so that exclusion should be presented as contextual clarification rather than as a change of problem statement.

To make the sum visibly polynomial-valued, it is best to say that M(u,v) is finite (or equivalently that only finitely many values of s occur), even though the displayed paper statement leaves finiteness implicit.
No extra hypotheses should be added: the paper does not restrict to finite Coxeter groups, Weyl groups, type A, crystallographic cases, or positive characteristic variants.
refined_question: For every Coxeter system (W,S), with Bruhat order <= on W, and every pair u,v in W with u <= v, let P_{u,v}(q) in Z[q] denote the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial of W (equivalently P_{u,v}=P^{emptyset,-1}_{u,v}=P^{emptyset,q}_{u,v} in the notation of Theorem 1.3). Does there exist an explicit, genuinely combinatorial, non-recursive construction that assigns to each interval [u,v] a finite set M(u,v) and a statistic s:M(u,v)->N such that P_{u,v}(q)=sum_{a in M(u,v)} q^{s(a)}?
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 1.10 in Section 1, not at the combinatorial invariance conjectures or at the type-A hypercube-decomposition conjecture. The displayed formula in your draft matches equation (1.4) attached to Problem 1.10 almost verbatim, and the added insistence on a genuinely combinatorial rather than recursive construction is supported by the paragraph immediately after Problem 1.10, where Brenti notes that Deodhar’s recursive construction of sets M(u,v) is for that reason not generally regarded as a combinatorial interpretation. To make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must identify P_{u,v} as the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial coming from Theorem 1.3 (with J=emptyset and x=-1 or q), retain the universal quantifiers over all Coxeter systems and all comparable pairs u <= v, and avoid broadening the scope to parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials or to the combinatorial invariance problem.
